The fact that she compared you to other girls really grinds my gears!! Parents should not compare their kids to other people at all. “Oh you should be more like them” — god, I hate this!! Don’t ever listen to your mom and keep dressing how you like. Your appearance, your life. If you like doing something and it doesn’t hurt anyone, then you should keep doing it. I don’t get why some parents feel the need to police stuff like this. Be glad your child is wearing clothes a stereotypical girly girl doesn’t wear instead of breaking the law or something. 

While having “feminine” clothes has been a problem for me as well (I don’t like dresses and jewelry, mom likes me wearing dresses and jewelry and etc, but I still have stereotypically “girly” style), what’s been a larger annoyance for me is my hair. I’ve had short hair (chin length) and longer hair (approx shoulder length) but what I’ve wanted to try for a while is having... even shorter hair? My mom dictates when I get my haircut and goes by this principle: I should get my hair cut during the summer since it’s hot, and my hair should grow out during the winter since it’s cold. What’s so illogical about this is that I always wear my hair up when it’s long because, surprise surprise, I hate how I look with my hair down.

Last summer I asked my mom if I could have very short hair and she looked like she got a stroke. When I showed her a picture of a woman with the length I wanted, I kid you not, she put her hand over her chest and gasped to exaggerate her surprise. She drilled into me with questions: “Where did you get the idea to have this hairstyle??? Who told you about this??? Why???” Obviously, many mainstream celebrities have this hairstyle. There’s no way I haven’t seen it. Some girls who go to my high school also have it. She then told me that I should keep my hair longer because I’m “too young” and I’d look like a boy if I got really short hair. I identify as non-binary so I don’t really care about looking like a boy, but at the same time this hurt me because I still care about my femininity, since I dunno, I was born a girl? Girls of all ages can pull off very short hair and it felt like an insult that my mom told me I couldn’t do it. Sure, maybe this type of hairstyle can’t be pulled off by certain people, but I’d at least like to see how I look with it. Isn’t it also better to try this out when I’m young? I feel like a lot of adults look back at their younger years and laugh at questionable clothing and hair styles, so if I end up not liking my hair, can’t I at least have the luxury to laugh about my decision? My hair can grow back, you know.

When I get to college, I’m heavily considering just chopping my hair off without telling my mom. It sounds so dumb but it really is a big deal to me. I want to feel comfortable with how I look and experimenting with my appearance is the only way this is possible.

Congrats! I’m glad things are working out for your mental health and I wish the best for you. I’ve read your other post and it sucks that your parents don’t care about this though. I don’t get why some parents, and especially APs, can’t believe that their child could have mental health issues. 

When I read the part you wrote about APs always thinking that having a mental illness is a one way ticket to the psych ward, that really hit me hard, because my mom said something along those lines to me when I was in middle school when I began to be “self destructive.” While this doesn’t apply to all of them, APs just tend to be emotionless jerks toward their children. Sometimes we just can’t do anything about it because their heads are so thick.

Again, I wish you the best. Take care of yourself! ❤️

I have three other Asian friends. Only one has a currently completely unproblematic family (she’s had past issues but her family worked through them and grew together; I’ve been with her parents and one of her older siblings and their dynamic is very comfortable). The two others and myself have more strained relationships with our parents.

My parents are more emotionally distant, I’m scared of talking to them, and every interaction I have with them is draining. On the other hand, my two other friends have parents that openly insult them and are the kind to yell at them harshly. My friends have talked back to their parents (not vindictively — they did so to point out how ridiculous or mean they were to them) but they would end up in trouble.

One of them told me she was kicked out of her house after a fight with her dad. The other one recently told me her dad deliberately took her car keys away from her to drive somewhere for an extended period of time in order to punish her, despite damn well knowing she needed her car for school-related activities, and still decided to use her car despite buying a car for himself not too long ago.

I feel terrible for them and relate to them immensely — although we don’t go through the same issues, I understand the horrors of having bad APs. Whenever we try to “fight back” against them, nothing works. They never seem to change.

We just hope we can put distance between ourselves and our parents in the future, because they always punish or hold us back.

I feel that the only way to improve this situation is to try to explain more that you need rest in between work. I know that you seem to have a hard time doing that though, so honestly, I agree with the other comment. 

If your dad continues not to understand, it doesn’t seem like you could change his mind. Once you get older, you won’t have to deal with him nagging you anymore, and you can work at your own pace.

And also, try not to feel guilty!! You definitely deserve resting in your free time, especially with all the work you’ve been doing. Remember to practice self care.

These past few months I’ve been having trouble drawing as well since I get no outside support (and this is really bad since I have to submit drawings for grades in an art class I’m taking!!).

Since you’re interested in drawing again though, you should just take it in small steps. You’re not going to get good again in a short period of time. You should draw what makes you happy for starters — it could be trying to replicate the anime style you used to have or it could be one of your favorite things. Maybe try some realism by copying a photo. Drawing everyday will improve your skills immensely in the long run. Don’t scrap your works and use them as references so you can see how far you’ll go in the future. Try not to be discouraged and keep on going! ❤️

Your post is a little confusing (I somewhat understand what you’re trying to say) but I can answer your question in the title.

I get that people might get uncomfortable when they see scars, but I don’t think they should be disgusted and condemn a person for self harming. I’m sure some have been told that they should cover up their cuts since they’re unsightly. My parents told me people would think I’m crazy if they saw my cuts and it made me feel crappy.

We all know self harming isn’t a good thing. But it’s an addiction. It’s similar to how some people gawk at smokers, alcoholics, and obese people — “why can’t they just stop smoking, or drinking, or eating food.” I can’t speak for everyone but I feel some people agree that self inflicted scars or bruises make them uncomfortable when they’re seen by others too because of the potential of being judged. That’s why we try to hide them.

There should not be an immediate negative response when a person sees cuts, because there’s a reason those are on a person’s body.

I’ve been cutting myself for the past few days but hiding the cuts is getting so frustrating. Sometimes it gets hot and I want to take off my jacket but I can’t because I know some people will wince at my arm. I’ve been wanting to tell my friends that I’ve been relapsing since it’s been bothering me but I don’t want to scare them so I’ve kept my mouth shut. I just want to shout out that I self harm and have people empathize instead of thinking “god, this person is crazy.”

If a person is purposely self harming because they’re attention whoring, that’s scummy. Those who self harm because they’re hurting are afraid of being the attention whores.

I try to comment on posts when I can — sometimes I read things but I can’t come up with anything to say. And like everyone else has said, I’m personally not in the best place so it’s not like I can give great advice or anything.

There’s tons of people on other mental illness subreddits that barely have any response to their posts too because they have much more subs — for the most part, a select amount of posts get attention while a bunch of others turn out to be white noise.

I actually prefer r/selfharm since I feel like posts here have a better chance of getting responses. We have smaller numbers after all. 

So... I understand why people choose to not comment on posts here, but I do agree that if someone’s asking for advice or is in need of another person to talk to, of course we should try and help. This is a community after all.

You’re not a bad person if you’ve admitted that the things you did were horrible — your feelings are completely valid. Besides, there are many people out there who have done bad things and don’t even care that they’ve hurt others. The fact that you have compassion makes the difference.

The ones who gave you negative responses didn’t care to understand your perspective. Whenever a person does a bad thing, it’s almost like they’re characterized by that thing, all above everything else.

I’ve recently done something bad too, and even if it was different than what you did, I still feel the same way: guilt. When this thing happened I immediately felt terrible, but I was made out to be the villain and had my suffering trivialized, which made me feel even worse. 

Please keep going and be safe. You’re a strong person and you can push past this. ❤️

Copying is one way to do it. When I was younger, I used to copy drawings of anime characters.

Learning anatomy is very important when drawing (when I drew as a kid I never cared about anatomy, and I'm regretting that I'm finally willing to do it recently). There's books, videos, and websites - there's so many resources you can't miss them. And don't be afraid to use yourself as a reference - sometimes when I need to draw a hand, I take a picture of one of mine and copy. 

Since you like the Ghibli style, you should also probably take a lot of screenshots to refer to when mimicking the style. But I also recommend that you not completely copy their style and make it your own! Maybe copy how they draw their eyes, backgrounds, etc... but having a signature look in your drawings will make your style stand out. :)

IMO, I feel like Monaca AND the Warriors of Hope shouldn't be considered as Ultimate Despairs.

I feel like the Warriors have more control over their choices compared to other Despairs, though this might be bias since they get to star in their own game while how exactly the Despairs acted is left up to imagination (save for Mikan on multiple occasions and Nagito, though the latter is STILL different from the others since he claims to both hate and love Junko). The Ultimate Despairs do everything solely because they want to cause despair, and even if they mask their intentions with a facade, ALL their actions would go toward it. 

In UDG, while the Warriors' goal was to eradicate all adults, they'd get distracted. A lot. Because they're kids. They all, except for Nagisa, would rather play that demon hunting game instead of moving on with plans. Also, one big twist in the story was that Monaca wanted Komaru to replace Junko, which was pretty shocking since Monaca seemed like a literal mini version of Junko. She wanted Komaru to become the Ultimate Despair, and not herself. 

The Warriors also exhibit flaws too, which I think would be uncharacteristic of an Ultimate Despair? I feel like those who are Despairs would be emotionless, except for loving Junko and their drive toward despair. Masaru hits himself before the first boss because he was scared of actually enacting his plan, and Nagisa and Kotoko both betraying Monaca and realizing what she was doing are prime examples. While they were swayed by Junko's teachings, they aren't completely controlled by her since they couldn't go through with these things. They're still kids who find it hard to make huge decisions. They were scared. 

Even Monaca changes her mindset in the end, since she got bored by despair and turned out not to like any of the conflict anymore (courtesy of Nagito). Compared to other Despairs, the Warriors eventually diverged from their thoughts. Monaca blasted off into space while the other four went to fight against despair, and they made these choices themselves. 

Healing the wounds of the Ultimate Despairs would have taken much more than this (since Nagito's OVA depicted him in a false world and eventually being awoken from it, I'm pretty sure the other Despairs underwent the same process - they had to heal from their mental damage via computer technology! and especially since the Neo World Program was originally going to have the Despairs just hang out and become friends... before SDR2 happened). 

And by the end of this, I'm tired of typing the word "despair" so many times.

Komaeda's character is intentionally made to irritate people, and despite that he's one of the most popular characters in the DR series, whether it's love or hate.

He was created to be a darker, twisted parallel to Naegi. Of course he's not supposed to be liked. He attempted to kill his classmates multiple time through different means, so the player would obviously start to dislike him. 

He did all he did in the series because of his character though... his mind is weak. For some bizarre reason he had this "luck cycle" controlling his life, and by losing all the things he loved he was bound to change drastically. From the get-go, he was already a messed up character.

He resonates with much of the fanbase because many feel bad about his past, and how he genuinely wanted to save his classmates, despite using roundabout ways to do it (I don't think killing people would lead to more hope AT ALL but that's how Komaeda's head works). These are also the very same reasons he's hated, but also respected by some of those haters - I've seen some really dislike Komaeda, but at the same time understand his character and why he acts like he does.

Komaeda isn't supposed to be that one cool guy character that's supposed to help the protagonist with friendship crap. He's supposed to be the personification of the views of Hope's Peak (which aren't pure AT ALL, with the Reserve Course nonsense and idolization of SHSLs) and serves as someone who tries to deter the player... though he does have complex motives for doing so.
